title: XML External Entity Injection Security Analysis

vulnerability.name: XML External Entity Injection
vulnerability.description: Attacks against applications that parse XML input
vulnerability.impact: File disclosure, SSRF, denial of service, or data theft
vulnerability.mitigation: Disable DTDs and external entities in XML parsers, validate and sanitize inputs

findings.title: XML External Entity Injection vulnerability
findings.explanation: The 'Bank' constructor calls an external contract, which may be vulnerable to XML External Entity Injection.
findings.impact: Potential remote code execution or data theft
exploitation_steps: Create an XML file containing a malicious DTD and reference it in the 'contract' parameter
Invoke the constructor, passing the malicious XML file as the 'contract'
Exploit the XML External Entity Injection to execute arbitrary code
findings.remediation: Disable DTD processing and sanitize input when constructing contracts
findings.secure_code_example: bank = new Bank({/* sanitized XML file */});

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The contract is not validating and sanitizing user-provided input, making it vulnerable to XML External Entity Injection.
findings.impact: An attacker can potentially manipulate the contract's credit assignment function.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
- User calls donate(address to) with malicious XML data
   - Contract parses and processes external entities in XML data
exploitation_steps: - Send maliciously crafted XML input to the donate function
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize user-provided inputs before processing them.

chunk_analyses.notes: Code is written in Solidity, an Ethereum smart contract programming language
